lead: “To follow in the footsteps of our late father, Sri Umakant.”
paras: ## Why is the trust dedicated to diabetes and metabolic disorders?
Is diabetes a significant and emotional issue? How widespread is the problem, and should we be concerned about its impact?
Yes, diabetes is also a deeply personal issue for us. We lost our father in 1987 due to diabetes-related complications.

According to Indian data, the number of people with metabolic disorders such as diabetes, prediabetes, hypertension, obesity, hyperlipidemia, and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease runs into millions. Nearly 15 to 20% of these patients suffer from microvascular (eyes, kidneys, and nerves) and macrovascular (cardiovascular disease) complications. Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease adds to the existing burden.

Greater diabetes awareness leads to better outcomes. Early diagnosis reduces the risk of complications and, with lifestyle changes, may help some individuals return to normal health. Improved knowledge among patients and healthcare professionals supports better monitoring, follow-up, and overall population health.

While treating metabolic disorders is possible, prevention remains the greater goal. Since chronic metabolic disorders can cause significant morbidity and mortality, ongoing education and familiarity with new technologies and treatments are essential for healthcare professionals.
Let us work together to make a meaningful difference in the lives of millions affected by metabolic disorders. Every contribution toward a healthier society is valuable.
umLead: Sri Umakant was a philanthropist and a man of principle. A former member of the Indian Air Force, he taught us through his actions to serve humanity.
umParas: He was a charter member of the Rotary Club of Sitapur when the club was formed in the year 1969. He was the charter president of the Rotary Club during the formation of the Rotaract Club in Sitapur district. He was also the Uttar Pradesh secretary of the Sri Aurobindo Ashram, Pondicherry, and an active member of the Annie Besant Society and the Theosophical Society in India.

Through the Rotary Club, he was closely involved in polio vaccination drives in the 1970s and early 1980s. He personally collected the polio drops from Lucknow airport, about 100 kilometres from Sitapur, and brought them in his own vehicle so that children could be vaccinated. He also took part in cataract eradication initiatives, under which many eye camps were held in the rural villages of Sitapur district.

mission: To help people with diabetes, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, and to train the medical and paramedical fraternity who care for them. Our objectives:

objectives.title: Medical education
objectives.text: Continuing medical education programmes and workshops for the medical and paramedical fraternity in Uttar Pradesh, on the latest technologies and drugs.

objectives.title: Free medical camps
objectives.text: Regular free camps for poor and needy people with diabetes, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases.

objectives.title: Free or concessional treatment
objectives.text: Supporting the treatment of poor patients and providing free or concessional medical treatment to the needy by setting up hospitals and medical institutions.

objectives.title: Students' education
objectives.text: Support for poor students' education by helping with fee payment and creating affordable educational institutions.

objectives.title: Greener environment
objectives.text: Facilitating tree plantation across Uttar Pradesh and the rest of India for a greener, healthier environment.

objectives.title: Rural upliftment and animal welfare
objectives.text: Work for the socio-economic upliftment of rural communities, along with animal welfare.
